source_name: Open Contracting Data Standard (standards + publisher registry)
licence: documentation under CC BY 4.0; the standard itself is openly published. Publisher data carries the publisher's own licence
historical_coverage: schema versions 1.0/1.1; publisher coverage varies by publisher
entity_identifiers: ocid (Open Contracting ID, the cross-publisher procurement identifier)
parties[].id (publisher-specific organisation id such as GB-FTS-188248)
known_limitations: This is a data standard plus a publisher registry, NOT a record publisher. It has no homogeneous record API of its own; searching it for contract records is a category error.
Actual records depend entirely on which publisher is used, and each publisher has its own endpoint, licence, latency and field population.

Field population differs by publisher: in the verified UK publication, awards[].date was null while contracts[].dateSigned was present - code written against the schema will run, but must not assume fields are populated.
The OCDS record model is the reason a single connector can be reused across publishers, so its value is as a design contract, not as data.
research_value: Defines the interoperability contract for procurement data: if a connector is written against OCDS release packages, the same normaliser works for any publisher (UK FTS verified, and other national portals use the same model). It is an architecture-level asset for MedRadar rather than a data source, and it is what makes the notice/award/contract stage tags portable.
cost_notes: free documentation and schema; publisher data costs vary
